w: This 5,822-metre stratovolcano rises just 12 kilometres from Arequipa, its double summit crater visible from nearly everywhere in the city. An active lava dome still vents gas inside the inner crater. Arequipa's suburbs have crept onto its lower slopes despite Misti ranking among the world's most dangerous volcanoes.
s: The volcano that looms over every Arequipa street
_facts: stratovolcano reaching 5,822 metres, 12 km from Arequipa
active lava dome vents gas inside the inner crater
last major eruptions around 2,000 years ago and 1440-1470 AD
considered one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world

w: Built largely from sillar, the pearly white volcanic stone that gives Arequipa its nickname of the White City, this suburb centres on a mirador beside a colonial-era church where crowds gather for the view: city rooftops with Misti and its neighbouring volcanoes filling the skyline behind.
s: Arequipa's white-stone mirador over the volcanoes
_facts: known for buildings built from sillar volcanic rock
home to the popular mirador e iglesia de Yanahuara viewpoint
surroundings hold Spanish-colonial-era churches and public parks

w: Thirty kilometres from Arequipa on the slopes of the volcano Pichu Pichu, this village built its Templo del Espiritu Santo in 1739, two centuries after Diego Hernandez de Cordova's 1540 arrival. Feathered angels flank its facade, cherubs ring the cornice, and four saints fill the dome's corners -- one of the era's most original church designs.
s: A remote colonial temple on Misti's sister volcano
_facts: village on the slopes of the volcano Pichu Pichu, 30 km from Arequipa
Templo del Espiritu Santo built from 1739
Spanish presence dates to emissary Diego Hernandez de Cordova in 1540
facade decorated with feathered angels, cherubs and four full-length saints

w: Facing the Plaza de Armas, this basilica is reckoned one of Peru's most unusual colonial cathedrals, and serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Arequipa. Architect Lucas Poblete is credited with the design, raised in the pale sillar stone that gives the city its white-washed look.
s: The white-stone cathedral anchoring Plaza de Armas
_facts: located on the Plaza de Armas of Arequipa
seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Arequipa
designed by architect Lucas Poblete
regarded as one of Peru's most unusual colonial cathedrals

w: UNESCO named Arequipa's colonial core a World Heritage Site in December 2000, calling its 'ornamented architecture' a masterpiece fusing European and native traditions. Raised in pale sillar stone below its volcanoes, the centre survived earthquakes, conquest and evangelism, keeping its Spanish-colonial character.
_facts: declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in December 2000
described as a masterpiece fusing European and native architectural traditions
shaped by earthquakes, indigenous influence, conquest and evangelism

w: Consecrated in 1579, this Dominican convent occupies an entire walled block of Arequipa, its cloisters, cells and cobbled lanes still standing behind fortress-like walls. It forms part of the same UNESCO World Heritage listing that covers the historic centre spreading out around it.
s: A walled 1579 convent hidden inside its own city block
_facts: Dominican Second Order monastery consecrated in 1579
occupies its own walled section of Arequipa
part of the UNESCO Historical Centre of the City of Arequipa listing

w: Domingo Carlos Tristan del Pozo commissioned this Andean Baroque mansion in 1738, its sillar facade carved in the ornate style that defines colonial Arequipa. Later known as the Ricketts House after a subsequent owner, it has belonged to the bank BBVA Peru since 1974.
s: An Andean Baroque mansion turned bank showcase
_facts: Spanish-era Andean Baroque house, construction begun 1738
commissioned by Domingo Carlos Tristan del Pozo
also known as the Ricketts House

n: Basilica and Convent of San Francisco de Arequipa
w: One of the largest churches in Arequipa's historic centre, San Francisco is built from tuff with a single-nave brick vault in the Andean Baroque style. Its convent complex holds a site museum, an art gallery and a library topping twenty thousand volumes -- a working archive as much as a place of worship.
s: A Franciscan basilica with a 20,000-volume library
